title: The influence of type 1 diabetes on cardiac function and oxygen uptake during exercise capacity in children and adolescents – The T1CKET Study
summary: The aim is to determine whether the metabolic changes caused by type 1 diabetes affect the oxygen cascade from the heart to the skeletal muscle during physical exertion, compared to healthy children and adolescents. To do this, the participants must complete an exercise test on a recumbent bicycle. Before, during, and after the test, blood parameters will be taken, blood pressure and muscle oxygen saturation will be measured, a continuous ECG will be recorded, and an echocardiogram will be performed at rest, during, and after exercise. All participants will wear a glucose sensor for 2-3 days before and after the exercise test.
conditions: Diabetes mellitus typ 1 with and without ketoacidose

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- T1D more than 5 years (only group A)
- Age 12-18 years
- No diabetic ketoacidosis in the last 6 months (only group A)
- Written consent from at least one parent/guardian
Exclusion criteria:
- Known heart defects such as hemodynamically relevant ventricular or atrial septal defect, transposition of the great arteries, aortic isthmus stenosis, tetralogy of Fallot, hypoplastic left heart syndrome, Ebstein anomaly, double aortic arch
- Pre-existing heart failure
- Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
- Cardiac arrhythmias
- Known arterial hypertension
- Known renal insufficiency
- Chronic pulmonary diseases: severe bronchial asthma, cystic fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension
- A history of cancer
- Pregnancy (clinical indication)
- Diabetic ketoacidosis within the last 6 months
